old_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene of a stormy sky over a vast, open landscape. Dark, ominous clouds dominate the upper portion of the frame. Rain is visible falling vertically from the clouds. The ground below is a flat, arid expanse with sparse vegetation, suggesting a desert or semi-arid region. In the distance, a range of low-lying mountains can be seen, adding depth to the landscape. The scene shows dynamic changes, including the shifting and intensifying rain curtain and dust kicked up by the wind, with visible movement of the clouds and changing lighting.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene of a stormy sky over a vast, open landscape. Dark, ominous clouds dominate the upper portion of the frame, gradually moving across the sky. As the video progresses, these clouds begin to release rain, which is visible as a thin line of precipitation moving horizontally from left to right. The ground below is a flat, arid expanse with sparse vegetation, suggesting a desert or semi-arid region. In the distance, a range of low-lying mountains can be seen, adding depth to the landscape. The lighting shifts subtly throughout the sequence, indicating the passage of time and the changing intensity of the storm. The overall atmosphere is one of tension and anticipation, as the storm seems to be gathering strength.
caption: The video captures a wide desert scrubland beneath a towering, dark storm cloud that dominates the sky. A broad gray column of rain or outflow descends from the cloud base near the center-left and touches the flat ground. Its lower portion is lit by a bright sunlit patch that persists throughout the excerpt. Along the right horizon, a low mountain range stands partly veiled by a tan dust band that thickens and rises well above the ridgeline. This dust front advances steadily leftward along the ground, spreading toward the center and increasingly obscuring the mountains. The base of the central column blends with the rising dust near the horizon, while the dark shelf overhead creeps subtly. The foreground shrubs and the camera viewpoint remain fixed, framing an ongoing storm process.

necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
